newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday because of two new domestic A share issues on the Shanghai stock exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 12.14 percent from 11.20 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell slightly to 8.3 million lots from 8.4 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said some big institutions borrowed heavily today to bid for the two new A share issues, pushing up the rates.
"The new issues boosted fund demand on the repo market, pushing up the rates, in particular those for the early-maturing contracts," said one trader.
"The pace of issuing new A shares is speeding up," he added. "This has been supporting the repo rates."
Traders said they expected the rates to move at the current high levels early next week due to further A share issues.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday with a fall on the domestic A share market pushing some liquidity back to the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 119.12 yuan from 119.00 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 1.22 million lots from 1.02 million lots.
Traders said the spot contracts were unlikely to go up sharply next week despite their high yields because daily volumes on the market had been thin this week, indicating prices lacked momentum.
